payload.feature:
Close issue #221: Muninn's two residuals from decision 0046 slice (i), accepted by the operator as residuals rather than a fourth return (proposal D34, 2026-09-06).

Read the issue, decision 0046 with its addendum and erratum, the archived change under `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-06-boundary-named-slice-i/` and the promoted specs it wrote under `openspec/specs/`.

**The two findings, both low, both one clause of work.**

1. **The delivery gate's check summary leaves one state unstated.** A manifest carrying both `hands` and `boundary` keys, with a journal that has no `effect/started.boundary` entry yet: the view renders `no boundary recorded` for that state and the script appends nothing. It is unreachable for a completed anchored run over any shipped bundle, since each runs a hands gate before `done` — so this is about the two surfaces saying the same thing, not about a live defect. Align them with one clause, and say in the code or its comment why the state is unreachable rather than implying it is expected.
2. **The gate-law requirement does not state the arm its own design carries.** `gate-boundary-policy` omits what design DD22 and task 6.10 both carry: a work-class chain site with hands under `open` is admitted asking no fragment of any link. One requirement sentence and a scenario, so the spec is the one copy of the law and the design is not the place the rule secretly lives.

**Build it so:** the spec is edited where standing truth lives, and where the archived change carries the same text, both copies agree — a promoted capability spec and its archive delta are never allowed to drift. The scenario is testable and tested. Nothing here changes what any boundary does; this slice makes the written law match the built machine.

Constraints, binding: do not edit `contracts/*.v1..v8`, `realms.v1..v3`, `seat-record.v1..v3`, `policy/phase-machine.json`, `reference/`, or `fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson`. Re-pin any witness or compose digest that moves. Any test driving a boxed step end to end skips under `BROKKR_HANDS_BOX`. Coverage is exact and literal.

Green before you finish: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, and both `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self` and `--bundle bundles/verify`. Do not push and do not open a pull request; the operator lands it. Say what you could not verify and what evidence you relied on.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],

    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. result.notes: 8 path(s) since b8078c6; outside the docs class: crates/brokkr-cli/tests/delivered_by_brokkr.rs crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/landing_shape.rs scripts/delivered-by-brokkr.sh

cargo test --workspace: 64 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed dbe6e4a (8 files) against b8078c6 and the #221 framing. Both clauses are built as asked and the change is behaviourally sound; three low findings remain, none security.

CORRECTNESS, verified. (1) The new jq branch `elif ($entries | length) == 0` sits after the `has("boundary")` test and before the malformed and unboxed tests, where both `any()` calls are vacuously false, so it masks no `unboxed`. I drove the whole rule through jq over all eight input shapes: no hands => nothing; hands without the boundary key, hands+boundary with zero entries, and a word outside the vocabulary => ' boundary not recorded'; a harness gate entry => ' unboxed'; namespace, a non-gate harness entry and the sentinel => nothing. Only the new branch produces the delivered assertion, so the test is load-bearing. (2) The alignment claim holds: brokkr-view's `run_boundary` (lib.rs:1422) renders NO_BOUNDARY on `declares_hands && no valid entry` without reading the manifest's boundary key at all, which is exactly the state the script now names. (3) The unreachability claim holds. `Engine::boundary_entries` (engine.rs:1236) returns None only when no site of the attempt declares hands, so any entry array carries at least one real word; and every shipped bundle's road to `done` passes a hands gate: preflight and bundles/verify enter at verify(gate,hands); landing enters at classify(gate,hands); research is research -> verify(gate,hands) -> done; self, fast, node and panel-review carry hands on verify and on ship. (4) The gate-law sentence matches bundle.rs:2205, where `SeatClass::Work` under `open` is an empty arm asking no fragment. (5) The promoted specs and the archived deltas differ only in the title line, the blank line and `## Requirements` vs `## ADDED Requirements` -- the bodies are identical, so no drift. (6) No frozen file, policy table, reference or corpus path is touched; no witness or compose digest moves (no production Rust line changed, engine version unchanged, the digest tests pass).

SIMPLICITY. Three consecutive branches now yield the same string; the split is deliberate and matches the file's case-by-case comment block, so I did not count it a finding.

SECURITY: none. `boundary_suffix` runs only after `verify_evidence` has chain-verified the journal and matched the anchor, so the manifest and entries it reads are tamper-evident; the new branch emits a fixed literal, so no journal-controlled text reaches the interpolated summary; and the change is strictly more conservative -- it converts a silence into an explicit absence and can never turn an `unboxed` run silent. The `commit.gpgsign=false` rider is scoped to one test fixture's own git argv and touches no production signing path. CI runs the base branch's copy of the script by design (ci.yml:71), so the new clause takes effect after merge; that is 0033 ruling 4, not a defect.

RESIDUAL FINDINGS, all low, none fixed (this seat is read-only).

- LOW, stale debt pointer. docs/decisions/0048-the-script-directory-is-the-spawn-pin.md:125, inside `## Consequences` (not a dated evidence section), still reads 'D34's delivery-summary absence case and missing explicit open-work delta scenario remain accepted residuals for Muninn.' Both are closed by this change, so an authoritative decision document now asserts open debt that no longer exists, and Muninn patrols exactly this list (decision 0020). The archived completion.md was amended correctly by appending a dated closure section; 0048 got no such line. In a slice whose thesis is that the written law matches the built machine, this is the one place the record still disagrees.

- LOW, undocumented out-of-scope rider. crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/landing_shape.rs gains `-c commit.gpgsign=false` on its git fixture. The fix is correct and genuinely needed -- this host carries `commit.gpgsign=true` globally, so the fixture #241 introduced would attempt to sign, and every other git fixture in the tree (anchor, keep_refs, hands, recipes, boundary_verbs, delivered_by_brokkr, ledger) disables signing for the same reason -- but it is named neither in the single-line commit message nor in the archived completion amendment, which enumerates every other part of the delivery. The durable record does not carry it; only the run's seat note does.

- LOW, scenario proven narrower than its sentence. The new gate-boundary-policy requirement says an open work-class site 'SHALL be admitted asking no fragment of any link' and the scenario's WHEN says 'a chain whose links declare no hands.harness fragment', but the binding test (model_policy_tests.rs:3163, `the_gate_law_reads_the_boundary_for_sites_that_declare_hands`) drives that arm only through `silent-box`, a single-link chain. The file already holds `falls-back`, a two-link fixture used for the harness gate arm, so a multi-link open work compile is one line away. A future per-link refusal that fired only on fallback links (the shape the gate chain rule already has) would slip past this scenario.

GREEN, run by me in this worktree: cargo fmt --all -- --check (clean); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings (clean); cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast (62 suites, all 'test result: ok', no failure, panic or error line); cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self and --bundle bundles/verify (both compile). Working tree still clean; I changed no file and made no commit.

COULD NOT VERIFY. `openspec validate --archived --strict` was refused by the sandbox's command policy, so I checked the archive-vs-promoted agreement by diff and the requirement/scenario structure by hand instead; the implementing seat reports it green. Exact coverage was not run -- it is host validation outside the box, and it is unaffected here because coverage-exact.sh excludes `tests/` paths from measurement (scripts/coverage-exact.sh:51) and this change adds no production Rust line. Remote CI on the final head is a handoff step with no result yet.
